results.title: On the third day of our visit to Nanning, I was honoured to be hosted by the Vice Mayor of Nanning City, Mr.
results.description:
On the third day of our visit to Nanning, I was honoured to be hosted by the Vice Mayor of Nanning City, Mr. Hou Jin, following our successful high-level engagement with His Excellency Wei Tao, Governor of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

Our engagement focused on initiating discussions towards establishing a Sister City Partnership between cities in Ghana and Nanning, with practical areas of collaboration in:

1. Urban planning and city development.
2. Development control and effective land-use management.
3. Urban transportation and mobility.
4. Education and institutional partnerships.
5. Healthcare delivery and medical cooperation.
6. Modern, AI-driven strategies for revenue mobilisation and efficient local governance.

We are particularly encouraged by the invitation extended to students from our respective cities to pursue academic programmes in our universities. We also explored opportunities for bilateral scholarship arrangements, university partnerships and academic exchanges.

We acknowledged the strong diplomatic and economic relations between Ghana and China, under the leadership of His Excellency President John Dramani Mahama and His Excellency President Xi Jinping of the People’s Republic of China. These high-level engagements provide an important foundation for translating bilateral relations into practical opportunities for our cities, institutions, businesses and people.

Our visit reinforces our commitment to building international partnerships that promote knowledge exchange, innovation, investment and sustainable urban development.

From diplomatic relations to practical partnerships, we are working to create opportunities that deliver tangible benefits to our people.

results.title: NAIMOS Arrests Chinese Nationals and Ghanaians Over Alleged Illegal Sand Winning at Asutsuare The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Se
results.description:
NAIMOS Arrests Chinese Nationals and Ghanaians Over Alleged Illegal Sand Winning at Asutsuare

The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has arrested some Chinese nationals and Ghanaians over their alleged involvement in illegal sand-winning activities at Asutsuare in the Greater Accra Region.

The arrests followed an operation by NAIMOS personnel targeting individuals suspected of engaging in unauthorised sand extraction in the area. The operation forms part of efforts to clamp down on illegal mining and other environmentally destructive activities across the country.

Illegal sand winning has raised concerns over environmental degradation, destruction of farmlands and the potential damage to water bodies and surrounding communities.
The suspects are expected to face the necessary legal processes as authorities continue efforts to combat illegal natural resource extraction.

🎥 3News

results.title: GCB Bank, in collaboration with the University of Cape Coast (UCC) Confucius Institute, successfully launched its Mandarin Language Training
results.description:
GCB Bank, in collaboration with the University of Cape Coast (UCC) Confucius Institute, successfully launched its Mandarin Language Training Programme on 6th November 2026 at Tang Palace.

Delivering the opening remarks, our Head of SOEs & Afro-Asia Banking, Aurelia Baaba Ofori Odame, highlighted the importance of language and cultural understanding in strengthening customer relationships and supporting trade and investment between Ghana and China.

She noted that the initiative forms part of GCB's broader Afro-Asia Banking strategy to equip staff with the skills to better serve Chinese-speaking clients and enhance customer experiences.

GCB Bank: Bridging cultures, strengthening partnerships and unlocking new opportunities!

results.title: Here's what the 4 major powers are currently doing in Africa.
results.description:
Here's what the 4 major powers are currently doing in Africa.

1.CHINA 🇨🇳
 Infrastructure & Loans.
The biggest player by far on the ground.

Building roads, railways (like Kenya's SGR), ports, dams, parliament buildings, stadiums under Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).

State-backed loans, Chinese companies build it, often with Chinese workers. $170+ billion lent since 2000.
Africa's largest trading partner since 2009. Buying oil, minerals, copper, cobalt. Selling phones, machinery, clothes.
Moving from big loans to smaller "small and beautiful" projects, green energy, and debt restructuring after Zambia, Ethiopia, Ghana debt crises.
■Praised for building fast, criticized for debt-trap diplomacy and bringing own labor

2.USA 🇺🇸 
Trade, Health & Security (but pulling back).
AGOA gave 32 African countries duty-free access to US market for 1,800+ products. Just announced termination of South Africa and Rwanda from Jan 2027.

PEPFAR spent $100bn+ on HIV/AIDS treatment in Africa, the biggest health program ever.

AFRICOM, drone bases in Djibouti, Niger (closed), training armies.

Prosper Africa initiative to encourage US companies to invest.
Much more transactional under Trump 2nd term,cutting aid (USAID cuts), demanding mineral deals, pressuring over foreign policy alignment (Russia, Israel, China).
■Praised for health aid, criticized for inconsistent attention and using sanctions

3. RUSSIA 🇷🇺 
Guns & Mining.
Russia's footprint grew hugely after 2020.
Wagner Group / Africa Corps. Security contractors in Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Central African Republic, Sudan, Libya. Provides regime protection after coups. Largest arms supplier to Africa selling jets, helicopters, rifles to Egypt, Algeria, Sudan, etc.

Deals for gold, diamonds, uranium in CAR, Mali, Niger.
Anti-colonial messaging "We never colonized Africa, unlike the West".
After Wagner mutiny, rebranded to state-controlled Africa Corps under Ministry of Defence.
■Welcomed by juntas for no-strings-attached security, criticized for human rights abuses and extracting resources

https://t.co/F6rg1IwvY4🇬🇧 
Finance, Aid & Soft Power.
Smaller than the other three but still influential.
Funding and insuring African mining, structuring deals.

FCDO aid focused on education, climate, girls' education. Big investor through British International Investment (BII).

Leverages large African diaspora in UK.
Post-Brexit trade deals, mainly with Kenya, South Africa, Egypt.

Cut aid budget from 0.7% to 0.5% of GDP, less direct infrastructure, more private sector investment.
■Praised for expertise in finance/law, criticized for declining engagement

China builds, America funds health and demands rules, Russia guards juntas and takes minerals, UK finances and advises. #Copied✍️
